title: UI unit-list comment and guard test name claim more than the static DOM guard checks (align with its exact patterns)
outcome:
Two pieces of wording overstate the static check "keeps every unit file free of Testing Library, rendering and the DOM globals" in ui/src/test-categories.test.ts:
- the comment above UNIT_TEST_FILES in ui/test-categories.ts ("rejects a unit file that imports Testing Library, renders, or uses the DOM globals itself");
- that test's own name.
The check matches only its listed patterns: a `from "@testing-library/…"` import, renderHook, render(, screen., document., window., and localStorage or sessionStorage. A side-effect Testing Library import, document['body'], navigator, location, requestAnimationFrame, the observers, `new Event` or createRoot(...).render( all pass it. docs/test.md and the guard's own comment already state those limits.

The same rewording can fix a Note from the same review: the vite.config.ts comment says the heavy and app files "either render the full App or exercise the scheduler-sensitive SessionPaneView and virtualizer lifecycle". src/panels/WorkPanel.test.tsx and src/panels/WorkTree.test.tsx are heavy because of measured duration and wall-clock waits, so the comment should add "or are CPU- or wall-clock-heavy".

This may be overtaken when the unit project moves to a node environment, which makes the static check a backstop only.
acceptance: The comment above UNIT_TEST_FILES and the guard test's name describe only what its patterns check (or name the patterns), consistent with docs/test.md.
The vite.config.ts comment on why heavy and app run in their own groups also covers files that are heavy by duration or wall-clock waits.
The full five-stage gate passes on the reviewed tree, and the review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher.
